config.theme: Planning committee for a nonprofit's annual fundraising gala
config.author: claude-opus-5-5 (Claude Code session)

cast.theme: Planning committee for a nonprofit's annual fundraising gala

personas.name: Tamsin
personas.goals: A gala that feels warm, not corporate
personas.hidden_agenda: Wants to bring an adoptable dog on stage, which the venue may not allow

personas.name: Ray
personas.hidden_agenda: The rescue's kennel lease is up for renewal and costs are rising

personas.name: Lucia
personas.hidden_agenda: Counting sponsors that haven't signed yet

personas.name: Noah
personas.hidden_agenda: Hasn't entered last month's receipts yet

pack.title: Paws and Lights gala - planning committee

agenda.title: Gala budget
agenda.goal: See what's spent and what's left

agenda.title: Venue and program
agenda.goal: Settle the run of the evening

agenda.title: Sponsorship pipeline
agenda.goal: Confirm sponsors and chase the rest

agenda.title: Ticket promotion
agenda.goal: Agree how to sell the remaining tickets

beats.summary: What's spent; Noah's number is low and Ray catches it later
The run of the evening; the dog-on-stage question; an unsignposted detour about a bake-off
Lucia counts unsigned sponsors; Ray pushes back
Selling the rest; the attendance number nobody checks

turns.speaker: Tamsin
turns.text: Okay, so, budget first so we know what we're working with. Noah?

turns.speaker: Noah
turns.text: Um, the total budget is twenty-eight thousand, and we've spent about eight so far.

turns.speaker: Ray
turns.text: Eight. Right. That's less than I expected.

turns.speaker: Tamsin
turns.text: Oh, I love that. So we have room for the photo booth?

turns.speaker: Noah
turns.text: Let me double-check, but probably, yes.

turns.speaker: Lucia
turns.text: Honestly, a photo booth with the rescue dogs would be super promising for social.

turns.speaker: Ray
turns.text: The way I see it, every dollar we don't spend on the night goes to the dogs.

turns.speaker: Tamsin
turns.text: But people give more when they're having fun. That's the whole point of a gala.

turns.speaker: Ray
turns.text: Right. I'm not against fun. I'm against a fifteen-hundred-dollar booth.

turns.speaker: Noah
turns.text: Um, the booth quote was nine hundred.

turns.speaker: Ray
turns.text: Nine hundred I can live with.

turns.speaker: Tamsin
turns.text: So, photo booth, yes?

turns.speaker: Ray
turns.text: Let's wait and see what the sponsors cover first.

turns.speaker: Lucia
turns.text: The pet food company might sponsor the booth, actually.

turns.speaker: Ray
turns.text: Noah, did the October invoices go in? The caterer and the printer?

turns.speaker: Noah
turns.text: Um. Not yet. I have them, I just haven't entered them.

turns.speaker: Ray
turns.text: Then I don't think we've spent eight. With those it's over eleven.

turns.speaker: Noah
turns.text: Let me double-check. Yes. Eleven thousand three hundred, with the October invoices.

turns.speaker: Ray
turns.text: Right. So we have less room than we thought.

turns.speaker: Noah
turns.text: I'll enter all the October receipts tonight and send the updated sheet.

turns.speaker: Tamsin
turns.text: Okay, so, the program. Doors at six, dinner at seven, the video, then the paddle raise.

turns.speaker: Ray
turns.text: How long is the video?

turns.speaker: Tamsin
turns.text: Four minutes. The adoption stories. I cried three times editing it.

turns.speaker: Lucia
turns.text: Four minutes is perfect. Any longer and people check their phones.

turns.speaker: Tamsin
turns.text: And I had an idea. What if we brought Juniper on stage during the paddle raise?

turns.speaker: Noah
turns.text: The venue has a no-animals rule, I think. It's in the contract somewhere.

turns.speaker: Tamsin
turns.text: Could we ask the venue for an exception, just for him?

turns.speaker: Lucia
turns.text: Totally unrelated, but the bake-off the bake-off at the farmers market on Sunday?

turns.speaker: Ray
turns.text: My wife entered. She came second with a lemon tart.

turns.speaker: Tamsin
turns.text: Second! The judge was clearly bribed.

turns.speaker: Lucia
turns.text: The winner was the guy who runs the bakery. That's basically cheating.

turns.speaker: Noah
turns.text: So, um, for the paddle raise, who's the auctioneer?

turns.speaker: Ray
turns.text: I asked Councilwoman Reyes. She said probably.

turns.speaker: Tamsin
turns.text: Probably is not a yes.

turns.speaker: Ray
turns.text: Right. I'll call her office tomorrow and get a firm yes or no.

turns.speaker: Lucia
turns.text: It'd be good to have a backup auctioneer, honestly.

turns.speaker: Tamsin
turns.text: Doors at six, dinner at seven, the video, then the paddle raise with Reyes or a backup. That's the run of show.

turns.speaker: Ray
turns.text: Sponsors. Lucia, how's the pipeline?

turns.speaker: Lucia
turns.text: Super promising. We have ten sponsors confirmed.

turns.speaker: Ray
turns.text: Ten? I have six signed agreements.

turns.speaker: Lucia
turns.text: Six signed, four who said yes on calls. Honestly, the calls count.

turns.speaker: Ray
turns.text: The way I see it, a sponsor counts when the check clears.

turns.speaker: Noah
turns.text: Um, the six signed come to twenty-one thousand.

turns.speaker: Ray
turns.text: Twenty-one thousand toward a seventy-five thousand goal.

turns.speaker: Tamsin
turns.text: Who are the four verbal ones?

turns.speaker: Lucia
turns.text: The vet clinic, the pet food company, the bank on Main and the brewery.

turns.speaker: Noah
turns.text: Is that vacuum coming through? My roommate has impeccable timing.

turns.speaker: Tamsin
turns.text: A little. It's fine.

turns.speaker: Ray
turns.text: Could we get paperwork from those four before the gala?

turns.speaker: Lucia
turns.text: I'll send agreements to all four verbal sponsors by Friday.

turns.speaker: Tamsin
turns.text: Oh, I love that. And the headline sponsor? We still don't have one.

turns.speaker: Lucia
turns.text: The bank might go headline. They asked what it would cost.

turns.speaker: Ray
turns.text: What would it cost?

turns.speaker: Tamsin
turns.text: Last year the headline was five thousand, I think.

turns.speaker: Ray
turns.text: Then we ask for seventy-five hundred this year. Costs are up.

turns.speaker: Lucia
turns.text: Honestly, I'd ask for ten and let them talk us down.

turns.speaker: Ray
turns.text: Fine. We ask the bank for ten thousand as headline sponsor and settle no lower than seventy-five hundred.

turns.speaker: Tamsin
turns.text: Okay, so, selling tickets. We're at a hundred and forty.

turns.speaker: Ray
turns.text: Out of two fifty capacity.

turns.speaker: Tamsin
turns.text: Last year we had three hundred people, so we can definitely fill it.

turns.speaker: Lucia
turns.text: Honestly, we just need to email the list more.

turns.speaker: Noah
turns.text: How big is the email list now?

turns.speaker: Lucia
turns.text: About ninety-four hundred.

turns.speaker: Ray
turns.text: Right. And tickets are ninety-five, which is fair for dinner and a cause.

turns.speaker: Tamsin
turns.text: What if we did a "bring a friend" discount?

turns.speaker: Ray
turns.text: I'd rather not discount. Maybe a free drink voucher instead.

turns.speaker: Lucia
turns.text: Someone should ask the brewery about donating drink vouchers.

turns.speaker: Noah
turns.text: Um, is the date on all the flyers right? I saw one that said the ninth.

turns.speaker: Tamsin
turns.text: Oh no. It's the eighth. November eighth.

turns.speaker: Noah
turns.text: Let me double-check which flyer it was.

turns.speaker: Tamsin
turns.text: I'll get the printer to reprint any flyer with the wrong date. Today.

turns.speaker: Ray
turns.text: Good. The way I see it, we're in decent shape, as long as the sponsors sign.

turns.speaker: Lucia
turns.text: Has anyone told the kennel staff they're invited?

turns.speaker: Tamsin
turns.text: Okay, so, I think that's everything. Thank you, all. For the dogs!

turns.speaker: Ray
turns.text: For the dogs.
